hero.description: Wat Phou Salao combines a working hilltop temple with Pakse's clearest city view: the large golden Buddha looks back across the Mekong toward the town and lowlands.
hero.rhythmNote: Come for the panorama, but remember that the viewpoint is part of a temple. The best visit gives both the city and the religious site a little space.
hero.photoNote: Across the Mekong from Pakse · Phou Salao

time.secondary: longer if you climb the staircase rather than drive up

budget.secondary: no standard admission fee; local donations may be possible

chapters.label: THE VIEW
chapters.title: The place that makes Pakse legible
chapters.body: From the hill, the Mekong stops being a strip at the edge of town and becomes the line that organises the whole landscape. The golden Buddha faces that view, with Pakse spread across the opposite bank. Late afternoon is the natural rhythm because the light changes faster than the site itself.

chapters.label: THE TEMPLE
chapters.title: Do not stop at the panorama
chapters.body: The seated Buddha is the obvious landmark, but the temple grounds continue beyond it. Give yourself enough time to walk rather than taking the view, one photograph and the road back. Wat Phou Salao works because it is both a religious place and a lookout.

note.label: ATLAS NOTE
note.text: If you want one short activity that explains where Pakse sits in the landscape, this is the most efficient choice.

items.label: Access
items.value: Staircase or road to the top
items.detail: After crossing the Lao-Nippon Bridge, you can climb the long staircase or take the road around the hill.

items.label: Best rhythm
items.detail: Sunset is the classic view, but arrive with enough daylight to walk around the temple before the light fades.

items.label: Time & entry
items.detail: Driving to the top makes the visit shorter; walking the stairs turns it into more of an outing. Current sources list no standard admission fee.

faq.question: Is Wat Phou Salao mainly a temple or a viewpoint?
faq.answer: Both. The giant golden Buddha and temple grounds are the religious focus, while the hill gives a broad view over the Mekong and Pakse.

faq.question: Can I drive to the top of Wat Phou Salao?
faq.answer: Yes. There is a road route around the hill, while a long staircase offers the more physical approach from below.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Wat Phou Salao?
faq.answer: Late afternoon is the strongest all-round choice because you can explore the temple in daylight and stay as the light changes over the Mekong.

faq.question: How long should I allow?
faq.answer: One to two hours is comfortable. Allow more of that time if you climb from below rather than driving to the upper parking area.
